authorities.citation: Securities Act of 1933 § 5, 15 U.S.C. § 77e
authorities.rule_or_holding: Prohibits offers and sales of securities through interstate commerce unless a registration statement is filed (offers) and effective (sales), subject to exemptions; prospectus delivery requirements.

authorities.citation: Securities Act of 1933 § 11, 15 U.S.C. § 77k
authorities.rule_or_holding: Express private right against issuer, signers, directors, underwriters and experts for material misstatements or omissions in an effective registration statement; issuer strictly liable; others have due-diligence defenses; statutory damages formula and negative-causation defense.

(a) device, scheme or artifice to defraud; (b) untrue statement of material fact or omission of material fact necessary to make statements made not misleading; (c) act, practice or course of business operating as fraud - in connection with purchase or sale.

authorities.citation: Application of the Federal Securities Laws to Certain Types of Crypto Assets, Rel. No. 33-11412 (Mar. 17, 2026), 91 Fed. Reg. 13714 (Mar. 23, 2026)
authorities.rule_or_holding: Five-category token taxonomy; explains how a non-security crypto asset may become subject to, and cease to be subject to, an investment contract under Howey; addresses mining, staking, wrapping, airdrops; supersedes 2019 staff framework.
authorities.validity_basis: Law-firm memos (Sullivan & Cromwell, Jones Day, Orrick; Mar.-Apr. 2026) and fintechlaw.ai report of Fed. Reg. publication; Corp Fin FAQs issued Sept. 25, 2026 (staff views).

authorities.citation: Semiannual Reporting, Proposed Rule (May 5, 2026), Fed. Reg. doc. 2026-09095
authorities.rule_or_holding: Would allow Exchange Act reporting companies to elect semiannual reports on new Form 10-S instead of quarterly 10-Qs.
authorities.validity_basis: Federal Register document 2026-09095 (proposed rule) and practitioner summaries (S&C, Deloitte, PwC) May 2026; no adoption found as of 2026-11-11.

authorities.citation: SEC v. W.J. Howey Co., 328 U.S. 293 (1946)
authorities.rule_or_holding: An investment contract is a contract, transaction or scheme involving an investment of money in a common enterprise with an expectation of profits from the efforts of others.

authorities.citation: SEC v. Ralston Purina Co., 346 U.S. 119 (1953)
authorities.rule_or_holding: The private-offering exemption turns on whether offerees need the protection of registration (can fend for themselves / access to registration-type information); the issuer bears the burden of proving an exemption.

authorities.citation: Omnicare, Inc. v. Laborers Dist. Council Constr. Indus. Pension Fund, 575 U.S. 175 (2015)
authorities.rule_or_holding: A statement of opinion is an untrue statement of fact under § 11 only if not sincerely held or containing an embedded false fact; it may be misleading by omission if it omits material facts about the issuer's inquiry or knowledge that conflict with what a reasonable investor would take from the statement in context.

authorities.citation: Slack Technologies, LLC v. Pirani, 598 U.S. 759 (2023)
authorities.rule_or_holding: § 11 requires a plaintiff to plead and prove that the securities purchased were registered under (traceable to) the allegedly defective registration statement.

authorities.citation: TSC Industries, Inc. v. Northway, Inc., 426 U.S. 438 (1976)
authorities.rule_or_holding: An omitted fact is material if there is a substantial likelihood a reasonable shareholder would consider it important - i.e., it would have significantly altered the total mix of information made available.

authorities.citation: Basic Inc. v. Levinson, 485 U.S. 224 (1988)
authorities.rule_or_holding: Adopts TSC materiality for 10b-5; contingent events assessed by probability and magnitude; rebuttable fraud-on-the-market presumption of reliance; silence absent a duty to disclose is not misleading.

authorities.citation: Matrixx Initiatives, Inc. v. Siracusano, 563 U.S. 27 (2011)
authorities.rule_or_holding: No bright-line rule that adverse-event reports must be statistically significant to be material; materiality is contextual.

authorities.citation: Ernst & Ernst v. Hochfelder, 425 U.S. 185 (1976)
authorities.rule_or_holding: Private 10b-5 liability requires scienter - a mental state embracing intent to deceive, manipulate or defraud; negligence is insufficient (recklessness question reserved).

authorities.citation: Tellabs, Inc. v. Makor Issues & Rights, Ltd., 551 U.S. 308 (2007)
authorities.rule_or_holding: Under the PSLRA, a 'strong inference' of scienter must be more than merely plausible - cogent and at least as compelling as any opposing inference, considering allegations holistically.

authorities.citation: Dura Pharmaceuticals, Inc. v. Broudo, 544 U.S. 336 (2005)
authorities.rule_or_holding: An inflated purchase price alone does not establish loss causation or economic loss; plaintiff must allege and prove a causal connection between the misrepresentation and the loss.

authorities.citation: Halliburton Co. v. Erica P. John Fund, Inc., 573 U.S. 258 (2014)
authorities.rule_or_holding: Declines to overrule Basic; defendants may rebut the presumption at class certification with evidence of no price impact.

authorities.citation: Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. v. Arkansas Teacher Retirement System, 594 U.S. 113 (2021)
authorities.rule_or_holding: Courts may consider the generic nature of statements in assessing price impact at class certification; defendants bear the burden of persuasion on lack of price impact; mismatch between generic front-end statements and specific back-end disclosures weakens inflation-maintenance inference.

authorities.citation: Central Bank of Denver, N.A. v. First Interstate Bank of Denver, N.A., 511 U.S. 164 (1994)
authorities.rule_or_holding: No private aiding-and-abetting liability under § 10(b).

authorities.citation: Janus Capital Group, Inc. v. First Derivative Traders, 564 U.S. 135 (2011)
authorities.rule_or_holding: The 'maker' of a statement under Rule 10b-5(b) is the person or entity with ultimate authority over its content and whether and how to communicate it.

authorities.citation: Macquarie Infrastructure Corp. v. Moab Partners, L.P., 601 U.S. 257 (2024)
authorities.rule_or_holding: Pure omissions (including failure to disclose information required by Item 303) are not actionable under Rule 10b-5(b); 10b-5(b) reaches half-truths that render statements made misleading.

authorities.citation: Chiarella v. United States, 445 U.S. 222 (1980)
authorities.rule_or_holding: Duty to disclose or abstain arises from a relationship of trust and confidence; mere possession of nonpublic information does not create a duty.

authorities.citation: Dirks v. SEC, 463 U.S. 646 (1983)
authorities.rule_or_holding: Tippee liability derives from the insider's breach; breach depends on whether the insider personally benefits from the disclosure; footnote recognizes constructive (temporary) insiders.

authorities.citation: United States v. O'Hagan, 521 U.S. 642 (1997)
authorities.rule_or_holding: Upholds the misappropriation theory (deceptive use of confidential information in breach of a duty owed to the source) and Rule 14e-3(a) as applied.

authorities.citation: Salman v. United States, 580 U.S. 39 (2016)
authorities.rule_or_holding: A gift of confidential information to a trading relative or friend satisfies Dirks' personal-benefit requirement.
Disgorgement is permissible equitable relief under § 21(d)(5) if it does not exceed net profits and is awarded for victims.

authorities.citation: SEC v. Jarkesy, 603 U.S. 109 (2024)
authorities.rule_or_holding: When the SEC seeks civil penalties for securities fraud, the Seventh Amendment entitles the defendant to a jury trial; the SEC may not adjudicate such claims in-house.

authorities.citation: Sripetch v. SEC, No. 25-466 (U.S. June 4, 2026)
authorities.rule_or_holding: The SEC need not prove that investors suffered pecuniary loss before obtaining disgorgement in a civil enforcement action (unanimous, Gorsuch, J.).

authorities.citation: SEC v. Govil, 86 F.4th 89 (2d Cir. 2023)
authorities.rule_or_holding: Second Circuit held disgorgement under § 21(d)(5)/(d)(7) requires a showing of pecuniary harm to victims.
authorities.validity_basis: Secondary sources (Harvard Law School Forum post June 20, 2026; Cooley June 22, 2026) report that Sripetch v. SEC (U.S. June 4, 2026) rejected the Second Circuit's investor-loss requirement. Confirm with citator.

evidence.limitations: Establishes the statement, not its falsity.
evidence.proposition: The FY2025 10-K stated that demand for the flagship product 'remains robust across all regions.'

evidence.limitations: Seasonality and contract timing could explain part of the decline.
evidence.proposition: Flagship backlog fell 31% from Q3 to Q4 FY2025 ($412.0m to $284.3m) per the notes to the audited statements.

evidence.strength_rationale: Timing suggestive; baseline trading pattern not yet compared.
evidence.proposition: CFO sold 120,000 shares in open-market sales (code S) on 2026-04-01, nine trading days before the corrective release; Form 4 not marked as a Rule 10b5-1 trade.
A short-seller report alleged management knew of order cancellations from the two largest customers by January 2026.
The company publicly denied that any top-ten customer cancelled orders before March 2026.

evidence.limitations: Timing of management knowledge not established.
evidence.proposition: Hypothesis: the 'robust demand' statement was a half-truth because management had backlog data showing a material decline when the 10-K was filed.
Q1 FY2026 release disclosed order cancellations in two regions and cut full-year revenue guidance by 18%.

evidence.strength_rationale: Undermines attribution of the whole decline to the corrective information.
evidence.proposition: The same release announced a CEO transition and a restructuring charge — potentially confounding information on the event day.

evidence.limitations: Synthetic data; no event study performed beyond market adjustment.
evidence.proposition: Synthetic demo price series shows a −14% market-adjusted move on 2026-04-15 (fictional).

issues.title: Rule 10b-5: 'robust demand' statements vs. declining backlog
issues.reach: Listed common stock; statements in periodic reports and calls.
issues.severity_rationale: Multiple statements over two quarters; 18% guidance cut.
issues.conclusion: Falsity and materiality reasonably supported; scienter contested; loss causation confounded by same-day CEO transition.
issues.open_questions: When did management receive Q4 backlog data? CFO trading baseline?

issues.title: Insider trading: CFO sales before corrective release
issues.open_questions: Was the CFO aware of cancellations on 2026-04-01?

issues.title: §11: 'on track' statement in prospectus while clinical hold notice pending
issues.reach: Follow-on offering under S-3; statements in the registration statement as of the takedown.
issues.conclusion: Strong falsity and materiality evidence; traceability likely satisfied for offering purchasers.

issues.title: §5 / §12(a)(1): unregistered token pre-sale

claims.plaintiff_arguments: Specific, verifiable demand statement contradicted by same-filing backlog data; repeated across call and 10-K.
claims.defense_arguments: Puffery ('robust'); backlog disclosed in notes (truth-on-the-market within the same filing).
claims.sec_considerations: SEC could also pursue negligence-based §17(a)(2) only if an offering occurred — none in window.
claims.scienter_analysis: Motive: CFO sales (not 10b5-1). Opportunity: certifications. Competing inference: seasonal backlog.
claims.causation_analysis: Corrective disclosure 2026-04-15 pre-open; confounded by CEO transition. Need disaggregation.
claims.unresolved: Internal knowledge timing; CFO trading baseline.

claims.plaintiff_arguments: Paired with 'across all regions' — a verifiable factual claim.
claims.defense_arguments: 'Robust' is a generalized statement of optimism.
CEO transition and restructuring explain the decline.
claims.causation_analysis: Market-adjusted move cannot be split without intraday data or analyst commentary.

claims.sec_considerations: Penalty up to 3× profit avoided; disgorgement (Sripetch).
claims.unresolved: Awareness of MNPI on trade date.

claims.plaintiff_arguments: Statement was untrue when the supplement became part of the registration statement; clinical hold notice received 2026-02-26.
claims.causation_analysis: §11(e) negative causation is the defendant's burden.

claims.provision: Token is a non-security digital commodity under the 2026 SEC taxonomy
claims.plaintiff_arguments: Pre-sale marketing emphasized team efforts and price; Howey governs.
